questions.question: Do the corrupt/truncated/unreadable image fixtures under tests/fixtures/images/ actually fail to decode when opened by the real image-decoding library used in production (verified independently of the test harness), or are they merely files named e.g. 'corrupt.jpg' that a permissive decoder opens successfully -- which would let the corresponding test pass regardless of whether the error-handling code path is ever exercised?

Could `references` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Does textbrush/references/ avoid importing backend, worker, or ipc (boundary rule 2, since references is a leaf shared by both composition roots), verified by an actual import-graph check of the new module rather than a manual code-review claim?

Is there a parameterized property test over non-square source dimensions (not just square test images) asserting the horizontal and vertical scale factors are exactly equal (not merely 'close' within a rounding tolerance), given that a per-axis-rounded scale factor differing by a few pixels is the specific gameable failure mode named for this story?

For a source image whose visible-content aspect ratio does not evenly divide the target canvas dimensions (forcing a rounding decision), does the test measure the aspect ratio of the un-padded content region specifically (not the padded output canvas), and does it assert exact equality with the source aspect ratio rather than an approximate/tolerance-based comparison?

Do the failure-class tests (unsupported extension, missing file, unreadable file, corrupt file, decode-resource-constrained) each independently trigger only their intended failure mode in isolation, and is the case-insensitive extension match (e.g. `.JPG`) tested against an actual file with that literal uppercase extension on disk rather than a lowercased path string constructed only in the test?

Is there a parameterized test across supported EXIF orientations and multiple non-square source dimensions asserting exact equal-axis scaling, aspect-ratio preservation measured on the content region, and full content retention, with production code (not the test) performing the actual EXIF/RGB/scale transform?

Is there a test proving centered-padding output is byte-identical across repeated runs of the same source+model+app-version, a test compositing an actual alpha-channel PNG onto the documented fill value with a pixel-level assertion, and a test that a resource-constrained decode raises an actionable error rather than silently producing a cropped/stretched/omitted result?

For each of unsupported-extension, missing-file, unreadable-file, corrupt-file, and decode-resource-failure, is there a test using a real fixture file exhibiting that exact failure mode (not a mocked open() call) asserting an actionable per-file error and that inference never starts, plus one uppercase-extension (.JPG) test proving case-insensitive acceptance?

Does a test assert the full NormalizedReference contract fields (pixel_data, width, height, content_aspect_ratio, fill_value, decoded_at) are all present and independently checkable on the return value of normalize(path) -- not just that pixel_data exists -- since S5 and S7 both consume this exact shape as the seam contract?

questions.answer: YES. scripts/generate_reference_fixtures.py generates every fixture and, before printing success, calls _assert_real_decode_failure() on corrupt_truncated.jpg/corrupt_not_an_image.png/corrupt_empty.jpg -- each opens via the real PIL.Image.open()+.load() path (the exact production decode call) and the generation script itself raises AssertionError if any of them decode successfully. It also calls _assert_real_decode_success() on every 'valid' fixture including unsupported_extension.bmp (proving that one is rejected on extension, not incidental decode failure). The script ran successfully (see result.json), so this was independently confirmed at fixture-generation time, not merely asserted in prose.
evidence: tests/test_references.py::TestFailureTaxonomy::test_unsupported_extension_real_decodable_file_rejected_by_extension (re-verifies via Image.open+load at test time too)

questions.answer: YES. textbrush/references/normalize.py and __init__.py import only `__future__`, stdlib (dataclasses, datetime, pathlib, importlib in tests only), and PIL. Zero textbrush.* internal imports exist in normalize.py; __init__.py's only internal import is its own sibling submodule textbrush.references.normalize. Verified by tests/test_references.py::TestModuleBoundary via AST parsing, not by reading the diff.

YES. tests/test_references.py::TestModuleBoundary reuses tests/test_config.py's _internal_imports() AST helper (the same helper S1 used and explicitly flagged as 'the template for S3's (references) ... leaf-boundary tests') against both textbrush/references/normalize.py and textbrush/references/__init__.py, asserting no import of textbrush.backend/worker/ipc (prefix-matched, not exact-string, per that helper's documented gotcha) and, more strongly, that normalize.py's internal-import set is empty.

YES. TestUniformScalingAndPadding::test_property_equal_axis_scale_over_arbitrary_dimensions is a Hypothesis @given property test over source_w/source_h/target_w/target_h in [20,900]x[20,900]x[32,512]x[32,512] (25 examples), asserting the measured content bounding box on the output canvas exactly equals round(source * single_scale_factor) on BOTH axes -- not within a tolerance. It also has 4 explicit non-square parameterized cases (landscape/portrait/square sources against square/portrait/4:3 targets) that assert exact equality, plus a dedicated odd-remainder tie-break test.

YES. test_content_aspect_ratio_measured_on_content_not_padded_canvas normalizes a 600x400 source onto a 500x500 (1:1) canvas -- a case that forces padding on one axis -- and asserts content_aspect_ratio == 600/400 exactly (pytest.approx for float division only, not a tolerance band on the ratio's correctness) and explicitly asserts it is NOT 1.0 (the padded canvas's ratio). test_all_seam_fields_present_and_correct performs the same exact-equality check on a non-square/non-square combination.

YES. Each failure-class test in TestFailureTaxonomy uses a distinct real fixture engineered to trigger exactly one failure mode (unsupported_extension.bmp is real+decodable, so only the extension check can reject it; corrupt_truncated.jpg/corrupt_not_an_image.png/corrupt_empty.jpg are three independently-caused corrupt-decode fixtures; the resource-constrained test lowers Pillow's real MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS guard against a real, otherwise-valid fixture, isolating that one mechanism). test_uppercase_extension_file_is_accepted uses tests/fixtures/images/IMG_1234.JPG, a real on-disk file whose suffix is literally '.JPG' (asserted via path.suffix == '.JPG' before calling normalize()), not a lowercased string built only in the test.

YES. TestExifOrientation::test_property_all_orientations_preserve_full_content_and_aspect is a Hypothesis property test over all 8 EXIF orientation tag values and non-square source dimensions in [20,400]x[20,400] (25 examples), writing a real JPEG with a real embedded EXIF Exif() orientation tag via PIL and asserting normalize()'s reported content_aspect_ratio matches PIL's own ImageOps.exif_transpose()-corrected dimensions -- i.e. production code (normalize()'s internal ImageOps.exif_transpose call) performs the actual transform; the test only uses exif_transpose independently to compute the expected value for comparison, not to perform the normalization under test.

YES, all three. test_repeated_normalization_is_byte_identical calls normalize() twice on the same source+target_size and asserts pixel_data.tobytes() equality (plus width/height/content_aspect_ratio/fill_value equality; decoded_at is deliberately excluded per the documented invariant). test_determinism_independent_of_max_image_pixels_headroom additionally proves the result does not change when more 'resource headroom' (a raised MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) is available. test_transparent_region_becomes_neutral_fill_not_undefined loads valid_alpha.png (real RGBA fixture, opaque-red left half / fully-transparent right half) and asserts pixel-level equality: opaque pixels keep their color unchanged, transparent pixels become exactly (128,128,128) -- not white, black, or undefined. test_decode_resource_constrained_raises_actionable_error and test_resource_constrained_failure_does_not_return_degraded_result cover the third: a real Pillow decompression-bomb guard trip raises ReferenceResourceConstrainedError and never returns a NormalizedReference (checked via a None-until-exception sentinel).

YES for all five failure classes using real fixtures (not mocked open()): unsupported extension (unsupported_extension.bmp, a real decodable BMP), missing file (a path that genuinely does not exist, constructed via tmp_path), unreadable file (a real file chmod'd 0o000 on disk, skipped only on non-POSIX or when running as root since root bypasses permission bits), corrupt file (three independently-sourced real corrupt fixtures: truncated JPEG, non-image garbage bytes, zero-byte file), and decode-resource-constrained (a real, valid, otherwise-normal PNG fixture decoded under a real lowered Pillow MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS guard -- the actual production safety mechanism firing, not a simulated failure). Plus the uppercase-extension case in VQ-S3-006's answer. Each asserts the specific matching exception type is raised (which necessarily means no NormalizedReference / no generation-eligible result is produced).

YES. test_all_seam_fields_present_and_correct independently asserts every field: pixel_data (type, mode=='RGB', size==target_size), width, height, content_aspect_ratio (exact expected value), fill_value (== NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE), and decoded_at (asserted to be a real parseable ISO-8601 string via datetime.fromisoformat, which raises if malformed).

questions.question: normalize()'s literal signature is normalize(path, target_size) rather than the single-argument normalize(path) written in stories.json's seam description. Is this deviation justified and does it preserve the frozen part of the seam contract (the NormalizedReference field list)?
questions.answer: SUPERSEDED by the remediation-round-1 VQ-S3-F2 record below: target_size was REQUIRED at the time this answer was written (normalize(path, target_size), no default), but round 1 (Decider ruling 2026-09-18, findings F1/F2) made it optional -- normalize(path, target_size=None). The reasoning about NormalizedReference's field list being preserved unchanged still holds, but this record's premise (target_size as a required argument) is stale; see VQ-S3-F2 for the current, accurate signature and rationale.

questions.question: Re-examination requested by Stage-1 review finding F8: the original post-impl YES answer to VQ-S3-004 rested on a property test (TestUniformScalingAndPadding::test_property_equal_axis_scale_over_arbitrary_dimensions) whose expectation re-derived production's exact clamp formula (`max(1, min(round(source*scale), target))`) verbatim, and whose input ranges (source 20-900, target 32-512) could never reach the degenerate case that formula's `max(1, ...)` was clamping -- so the test could not have caught a bug in that formula, and did not (see F5). Is the answer still YES now that both defects are fixed?
questions.answer: YES, now genuinely. The property test no longer restates `_scale_and_pad`'s internal formula: its expectation is an independent oracle checking the invariant the spec actually requires (measured content never exceeds the canvas; the per-axis scale factors implied by the MEASURED output pixels agree with each other within a rounding tolerance; the fit is 'contain'-tight against the bottleneck axis) rather than re-deriving production's pixel-count arithmetic. Its input ranges were also extended to source 1-4000 x 1-4000 against target 1-512 x 1-512, which does reach the degenerate case (verified: e.g. a 4000x3-shaped source against a small target triggers it within the explored space), and the test now branches to assert `NormalizationError` is raised there instead of silently computing an expected content size. A deterministic, non-randomized repro of the exact F5 report (4000x3 source, 512x512 target) is additionally pinned as its own test asserting the specific error and message content, independent of Hypothesis's example selection.

questions.question: F5 (sev 4, spec_violation): does `_scale_and_pad`'s `max(1, ...)` clamp silently stretch content for extreme source aspect ratios, contradicting spec.md sec 6.2's prohibition on silent stretching, and is this now fixed with an actionable error?
questions.answer: YES it was a real defect, and YES it is fixed. Repro before the fix: a 4000x3 source into a 512x512 canvas rendered content at 512x1 pixels (an actual 512:1 ratio) while `content_aspect_ratio` continued to report 1333.33 (the true 4000/3 ratio) -- a field lying about the pixels it accompanies. `_scale_and_pad` (textbrush/references/normalize.py) now raises `NormalizationError` naming the source and requested dimensions whenever either scaled axis would round below 1 pixel, instead of clamping. Verified live: normalize() on a 4000x3 PNG against target_size=(512, 512) now raises `NormalizationError: reference image 4000x3 cannot be scaled to fit within the requested 512x512 canvas: the extreme aspect ratio would round one axis down to 0 pixels (scale factor 0.128, computed content size 512x0)`.

questions.question: F4 (sev 5, incomplete_taxonomy): does `_decode` translate only the ERROR tier of Pillow's decompression-bomb guard, leaving the WARNING tier (roughly 1x-2x MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) to succeed silently or, under warnings-as-errors, escape as a bare `Warning` outside `ReferenceImageError`?
questions.answer: YES it was a real gap, and YES it is fixed. `_decode` now wraps the `Image.open()`/`.load()` call in `warnings.catch_warnings()` with `simplefilter('error', Image.DecompressionBombWarning)`, so both guard tiers raise and are caught, mapping to `ReferenceResourceConstrainedError`. Added a dedicated test using a 1.6x MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS ratio (within Pillow's own warning-only band, confirmed against Pillow's `_decompression_bomb_check` source: error above 2x, warning above 1x) which previously would not have raised anything.

questions.question: F3 (sev 6, mutable_seam_payload): does `@dataclass(frozen=True)` fail to protect the mutable `PIL.Image.Image` behind `pixel_data`, and does the auto-generated equality/hash mislead callers?
questions.answer: YES, confirmed, and addressed by contract statement rather than defensive copying. `frozen=True` only prevents rebinding `NormalizedReference`'s own fields; an external `.paste()`/`.putpixel()` on `pixel_data` still mutates the underlying PIL image in place, which would silently corrupt every later read of the same held instance under S7's decode-once lifetime (spec.md sec 6.3). The class docstring now states this as an explicit CONTRACT line (consumers must copy before mutating). Separately, `eq=False` removes the misleading default equality/hash (byte-identical images compared unequal by object identity; `hash()` raised TypeError on the unhashable `Image.info` dict) rather than leaving both to look like usable value semantics they were not. Deep-copying pixel_data on construction or access was deliberately rejected as the fix: it would add a per-generation memory cost to address a hazard the contract statement fully covers.

questions.question: F6 (sev 5, doc_inaccuracy): do normalize.py, architecture.json, and result.json all incorrectly state that spec.md sec 6.2 does not require the alpha-compositing fill and the padding fill to be the same value?
questions.answer: YES, all three were wrong and are now corrected. spec.md sec 6.2 states alpha sources are composited onto 'the same documented neutral fill' as padding -- a binding, not merely a permitted simplification. The code was already correct (one constant, NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE, used for both); only the prose describing it as an optional implementer choice was backwards, and a later story reading the old prose could legitimately have split the constants and violated sec 6.2 without realizing it. All three artifacts now cite the binding directly (ledger concept neutral-fill-binding).

questions.question: F7 (sev 4, weak_guard): since every fill-color assertion in tests/test_references.py derives `_FILL_RGB` from the imported `NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE`, would changing that constant to any other value still pass the whole suite?
questions.answer: YES it was a real gap (before this round, no test pinned the constant's actual value), and YES it is now fixed by a dedicated test asserting `NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE == 128`. Note: 128 does not yet appear in any user-facing documentation, so this test pins the constant against the spec's own requirement of a single *documented* value without yet having a doc artifact to point at -- closing that gap (AC-DOC-1) is S13's responsibility, out of this leaf-module story's scope, and is called out here rather than addressed unilaterally.

questions.question: F2 (sev 5, contract_shape), resolved by Decider ruling 2 (2026-09-18): is `target_size` now optional (`tuple[int, int] | None = None`), with `None` applying only EXIF orientation, RGB conversion, and alpha compositing (no scale, no pad), and is this covered by tests?
questions.answer: YES. normalize()'s signature is now `normalize(path, target_size=None)`. The None path is covered for: source dimensions returned unscaled/unpadded, EXIF orientation still applied (verified against the same rotated fixture used for the target_size-given EXIF test), alpha still composited onto NEUTRAL_FILL_VALUE, no fill-colored padding introduced (bounding box spans the full output), target_size being omitted entirely behaving identically to passing None explicitly, and NormalizationError never being raised on the None path (the scale/pad stage does not run at all -- verified by monkeypatching `_scale_and_pad` to assert it is never called).

questions.question: F1 (sev 6, unowned_dependency): did architecture.json's signature_decision and normalize()'s docstring incorrectly attribute reference-input-dimension derivation to S2's per-model registry data, when `ModelSpec` (textbrush/model/registry.py) has no dimension field?
questions.answer: YES, the prior attribution was factually false and is now corrected in both places. The fact 'model X's pipeline accepts reference inputs at dimensions D' is owned by `inference` (S5), exposed as a `reference_input_size(output_width, output_height) -> tuple[int, int] | None` accessor on the `InferenceEngine` instance per stories.json blocking condition S5-BC-1 (already reflected in stories.json/ownership-ledger.json by the lead; this story's part was correcting the false attribution in architecture.json and the normalize() docstring, both done). S7 is the pass-through conduit: it reads S5's accessor and supplies the resulting tuple to normalize() as a plain value. `references` continues to import neither `model` nor `inference`.
